indicators.note: the clue tells us to say the contraction out loud and write what we hear

parts.note: the contraction for I will, pronounced like a church walkway

explanation.surface: Someone announces they will recite a passage of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' looks like a stretch of writing to read, but it is the walkway between seats; 'read aloud' marks the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangway between rows of seats in a church or plane is a passage for walking.

clue.text: Spear-carrier in a fight with a theatre cat

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do in practice
Gus is the Theatre Cat in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum poems and the musical Cats

explanation.surface: A minor actor with a spear gets into a scrap with a feline.
explanation.walkthrough: A spear-carrier is a walk-on actor, but here it is a vegetable that grows spears.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable produces edible shoots called spears, so it is jokingly a carrier of spears.

clue.text: Make oneself scarce, having upset the brandies

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape residue, plural marcs

explanation.surface: Someone flees after knocking over the brandy glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MARCS around to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear off quickly is an informal command or verb for leaving at once.

definitions.meaning: Henry VIII's daughter became Queen of England in 1558
a reigning monarch, as each queen of that name was

explanation.surface: A king's daughter is handed a gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link; a sovereign is also a gold coin, which is the surface's misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to Henry VIII's daughter, who reigned as queen, a sovereign.

definitions.meaning: the hunchback who rings the bells of Notre-Dame in Victor Hugo's novel
the Sunday after Easter, named from the Latin introit beginning ... geniti

explanation.surface: A church needs someone to ring for the quiet Sunday service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required for' is a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugo's hunchback was named after the feast day on which he was found, the Sunday after Easter.

definitions.meaning: Adela ... is the young Englishwoman in E. M. Forster's A Passage to India

explanation.surface: Someone went looking for a woman called Adela in India.
explanation.definitionFit: To quest is to seek; Forster's heroine in India bears this surname.

parts.note: a TU, trade union, is the workers as a body
ate means swallowed food

explanation.surface: An accountant's report was accepted by the union.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something in motion or motivate is to drive or inspire it.

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is goes around the betrayer

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is
to rat is to desert one's side

explanation.surface: A desert is described as boiling hot all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a sandy place but is the verb, to abandon, giving RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiling with rage means furious, very angry.

clue.text: Stay out longer than one intended

definitions.text: Stay out longer than one intended

parts.words: Stay out longer than one intended
parts.note: reads like staying out late at a party, but describes staying asleep beyond the time one meant to wake

explanation.definitionFit: Sleeping past one's planned waking time means remaining in bed too long.

indicators.note: errant means wandering, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone worships a wandering nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'errant' rearranges ADORE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is a mountain nymph.

definitions.meaning: appropriate, apt to the matter in hand

explanation.surface: Cloth is ready for a dressmaker's fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'available for' is a link joining two definitions; 'Material' and 'fitting' are not the cloth and the dress session.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevant and apt to the point, as material evidence is relevant.

clue.text: Piece of bare terrain in part of mountain range

indicators.note: a piece of the phrase is taken, letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A patch of bare ground lies in a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of' marks the hidden run in b(ARE TE)rrain.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp mountain ridge is a feature of a range.

clue.text: After the game, doctor goes to a dance

indicators.note: after says the doctor follows the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: After the match the team doctor goes to a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance of this name.

clue.text: Farcical playwright, English, died — or passed over

parts.note: Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces of the 1920s

explanation.surface: An English farce writer has died, or merely been overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link; 'passed over' means crossed, not ignored as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross a stretch of ground is to pass over it.

clue.text: Gallery object is a welcome acquisition

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery in a theatre
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A piece bought for an art gallery is a welcome purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gallery' is the theatre's top tier, not an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heaven-sent arriving just when needed is a welcome gain.

indicators.note: sounding says the words are judged by how they are pronounced

parts.note: dire means grim; said aloud in a non-rhotic accent it is heard as dia
a critic is a commentator; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A bleak-voiced pundit's accent is an example of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' marks the homophone on DIRE alone: said aloud it gives DIA, then CRITIC follows as written.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent mark over a letter is one example of a mark altering its pronunciation.

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of
a press is a crowd or throng

explanation.surface: A voice rises out of the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to put it into words, articulate it.

parts.note: the press is the newspapers

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the reading word is cut off

parts.note: study is careful perusal

explanation.surface: A newspaper reader studies the papers at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the Y of STUDY; 'Popper' is not the philosopher but a snap fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A popper is the British name for a snap fastener on clothing.

clue.text: Discarded metal club propping up shed

indicators.note: in a down clue, propping up puts the club below the other piece

parts.note: to scrap is to shed or discard
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A golf club is used to prop up a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' is a verb, to discard, not a garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste metal thrown away for recycling is this.

definitions.meaning: slang for a very attractive person, a dish

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a breaker of things, and British slang for a stunning person.

clue.text: Put out again in new university series

indicators.note: in says the university letter goes inside the rearranged word
new says the letters of the next word are made into something new

explanation.surface: A university launches a new series of lectures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SERIES to REISSE, and 'in' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Publishing again, as a new edition is published again.

definitions.meaning: a small hoop earring worn to keep a pierced ear open
an agent planted to lie dormant until activated

explanation.surface: A dormant spy might be a member of a spy ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a small earring and a dormant agent go by this name.

clue.text: Conspicuous foreigner getting in the way

indicators.note: getting in says the foreigner goes inside the street

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
an alien is a foreigner

explanation.surface: An obvious foreigner obstructs the path.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient feature is prominent, standing out.

indicators.note: can be says the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Country mice are full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges RURAL MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick-changing and spirited, like the metal quicksilver.

indicators.note: in a down clue, pile-up means the letters are stacked from the bottom upwards

parts.note: some means a little, as in some milk

explanation.surface: Notes record a small crash on a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pile-up' turns SOMEM upwards in the down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Short written notes kept as records.

indicators.note: upset says the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Muslim doctor knocks over a mule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges A MULE.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor of Islamic law and theology belongs to this learned body; the word is used for one scholar too.

clue.text: Team kit that may be torn off in anger?

definitions.text: that may be torn off in anger?
definitions.meaning: to tear someone off one of these is to scold them angrily

explanation.surface: A footballer rips off his shirt in a fit of rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A football team's uniform, and the thing torn off a person in a telling-off.

indicators.note: not ending says the final letter of the portion is dropped

parts.note: a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: A relationship needs support but not a breakup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ending' cuts the N from RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion between two quantities is a numerical relationship.

clue.text: Unit in which Frenchman may measure his length

definitions.text: Unit in which Frenchman may measure his length

parts.words: Unit in which Frenchman may measure his length
parts.note: describes the metric measure of length used in France rather than feet

explanation.definitionFit: The basic metric unit of length used in France.

clue.text: Part of gate that's given weekly inspection?

definitions.text: Part of gate that's given weekly inspection?

parts.words: Part of gate that's given weekly inspection?
parts.note: one of the crowd at a match, the gate, and a weekly magazine scrutinising the news

explanation.definitionFit: A member of the paying crowd watching a match, and a British weekly magazine.

clue.text: Religious ceremony in state capital ending prematurely

indicators.note: the last letter of the city is cut off early

parts.note: Sacramento is the capital of California

explanation.surface: A church service is held in a state capital but ends early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending prematurely' drops the final O of SACRAMENTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christian rite such as baptism or communion.

clue.text: Depressed about onset of recession, go under

indicators.note: about says the gloomy word wraps round the letter

parts.note: down means depressed

indicators.note: onset is the start, so the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Feeling gloomy at the start of a recession, a business goes under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onset of' gives R, which 'about' puts inside DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To go under water and suffocate.
